observation: Bulk data replication across multiple cloud regions and providers is essential for data analytics, disaster recovery, and geo-distributed model serving, yet cloud multicast can be expensive due to per-GB network egress fees and slow due to cloud network constraints. Egress prices vary by up to 23× across region pairs, with intra-cloud egress costing $0.01–$0.19 per GB and inter-cloud egress costing $0.08–$0.23 per GB, and cross-region bandwidth varies by up to 202×. Cloud providers impose per-VM egress/ingress limits (for example, AWS throttles egress to 5 Gbps per VM), so a single source VM is often the bottleneck, while users must still meet target replication times. Existing throughput-oriented multicast optimizers do not handle monetary cost, and existing cost-aware multicast work either ignores throughput or assumes a capacity-based pricing model that is inconsistent with today's per-GB egress pricing.

claims: Application-layer multicast builds overlay trees or meshes to deliver data to many receivers and optimizes the overlay for aggregate throughput or end-to-end delay rather than monetary cost.
Throughput-centric overlay multicast does not model the egress fees that clouds charge when traffic leaves a region or a provider.
Peer-assisted file dissemination protocols deliberately engage the upload bandwidth of multiple helper nodes so that a single source VM is not the throughput bottleneck.

claims: Minimum-cost multicast with network coding is formulated over capacitated links in which each link has a cost per unit of carried rate, and the task is to find a minimum-cost subgraph for a fixed multicast rate.
This capacity-based cost model is inconsistent with per-byte egress fees that vary by destination region and provider, and it does not decide throughput jointly with cost.

claims: Geo-distributed analytics schedulers incorporate monetary cost into their data-placement and query-routing decisions.

Those schedulers are scoped to repeated analytical queries and do not address one-time bulk replication of large datasets to a user-specified set of cloud regions and providers under per-VM bandwidth caps and per-GB charges.
